answerStage.answerDesign: 정답 문장인 'This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment that is shown in his artwork.'에서 관계대명사절 내의 수동태 형태인 'is shown'을 능동태 형태인 'shows'로 변형하여 오류를 생성합니다. 관계대명사 that은 선행사인 an attachment를 가리키고, 예술작품 속에서 이 애착이 '보여지는(수동)' 것이 논리적이고 문법적으로 올바릅니다. 만약 'shows'로 쓰면 타동사 show의 목적어가 빠진 채 능동태가 유지되므로 문법적으로 불완전한 비문이 됩니다. 선행사 관계를 고려했을 때 다른 해석으로 읽어도 능동태 'shows'는 비문입니다.

answer.surroundingText: This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment that is shown in his artwork.

answerStage.explanation: 관계대명사 that의 선행사는 'an attachment(애착)'입니다. 애착은 그의 예술작품 속에서 '보여지는' 대상이므로 수동의 관계가 성립합니다. 따라서 능동태인 shows를 쓰면 타동사 show의 목적어가 없는 불안정한 문장이 되므로, 수동태인 is shown으로 표현하는 것이 올바릅니다.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment that is shown in his artwork.

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: During World War II, he traveled to California, where he became interested in the media of sculpture.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Houser's designs are modern, yet firmly rooted in the special tradition of his Native American forefathers.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The sculpture Reverie shows a distinct Native American influence, but it can be appreciated by anyone, regardless of his or her background.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 시간을 나타내는 부사절(As a child) 뒤에서 주어(he)에 이어지는 주절의 정동사 과거형으로, 문장의 시간적 배경과 일치하여 올바르게 쓰였습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 장소를 뜻하는 선행사 California를 부가적으로 수식하는 관계부사이며, 뒤에 완전한 문장 구조가 뒤따르고 있으므로 어법상 적절합니다.

question.explanation: 관계대명사 that 뒤에서 선행사인 'an attachment(애착)'가 예술작품 속에서 '보여지는' 대상이 되므로 수동의 관계가 성립합니다. 따라서 능동태인 shows를 쓰면 타동사 show의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 문장이 되므로, 수동 형태인 is shown으로 고쳐야 올바른 문장이 됩니다. 수동태 뒤에 목적어가 결여된 자연스러운 구조를 파악하는 것이 핵심입니다.
keyPoints: (B) 능동태 vs 수동태 — 선행사와의 의미 관계 및 목적어 유무로 판정
(C) 관계부사 vs 관계대명사 — 뒷문장의 완전성 여부로 판정
(D) 현재분사 vs 과거분사 — 주어와의 수동 수식 관계로 판정
question.passageWithMarkers: Allan Houser created contemporary Apache sculpture. As a child, he __(A) listened__ to his father's stories about the adventures of Chief Geronimo. This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment that __(B) shows__ in his artwork. Houser studied at the Indian School in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and then remained in Santa Fe, where he worked as a freelance artist. During World War II, he traveled to California, __(C) where__ he became interested in the media of sculpture. He created works in a variety of styles and mastered bronze, metal, and stone sculpture. Houser's designs are modern, yet firmly __(D) rooted__ in the special tradition of his Native American forefathers. He drew inspiration from both past and present, but like all successful artists, his sculpture transcends race and language. The sculpture Reverie shows a distinct Native American influence, but it can be appreciated by anyone, __(E) regardless of__ his or her background.

passageText: Allan Houser created contemporary Apache sculpture. As a child, he listened to his father's stories about the adventures of Chief Geronimo. This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment that is shown in his artwork. Houser studied at the Indian School in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and then remained in Santa Fe, where he worked as a freelance artist. During World War II, he traveled to California, where he became interested in the media of sculpture. He created works in a variety of styles and mastered bronze, metal, and stone sculpture. Houser's designs are modern, yet firmly rooted in the special tradition of his Native American forefathers. He drew inspiration from both past and present, but like all successful artists, his sculpture transcends race and language. The sculpture Reverie shows a distinct Native American influence, but it can be appreciated by anyone, regardless of his or her background.

answerStage.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
answerStage.answerDesign: 정답 문장인 'Next time you look up, you'll see someone else similarly immersed...'에서 'immersed'를 현재분사 형태인 'immersing'으로 변형합니다. 지문에서 'someone else'가 'immersed(몰입된)' 상태인 것을 지각동사 'see'의 목적격 보어로 서술해야 하므로 수동 의미의 과거분사 'immersed'가 필요합니다. 주체인 'someone else'가 책읽기에 무언가를 몰입시키는 동작을 능동적으로 행하는 대상을 가리킬 수 없으므로, 'immersing'으로 쓰면 통사적/의미적으로 비문이 됩니다. 이는 다른 성분 분석으로도 정문이 될 수 없는 명백한 수동 분사 자리입니다.

answer.surroundingText: Next time you look up, you'll see someone else similarly immersed, and you won't feel alone at all.

answerStage.explanation: 지각동사 see의 목적어인 someone else와 목적격 보어의 관계는 수동입니다. 누군가가 (독서 등에) '몰입된' 상태임을 나타내므로, 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거분사 immersed가 와야 올바릅니다. 능동을 뜻하는 현재분사 immersing을 쓰면 문맥상 어색할 뿐만 아니라 문법적으로 옳지 않습니다.

wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 선행사인 people을 수식하며 주어 역할을 하는 주격 관계대명사 who가 바르게 쓰였습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 선행사 a reading group을 수식하며, 전치사+관계대명사 뒤에 완전한 절(everybody takes turns...)이 이어지고 있으므로 어법상 적절합니다.

keyPoints: (C) 분사의 능동 vs 수동 — 지각동사 목적격 보어 자리에서 대상의 수동적 상황 판정
(A) 능동태 vs 수동태 — 전치사 뒤에서 남겨지는 수동적 행위이므로 동명사 수동태 사용
(D) 관계대명사 vs 전치사+관계대명사 — 관계사절의 구조가 완전한지 불완전한지 구별
question.passageWithMarkers: We all enjoy the pleasure of __(A) being left__ alone with a good book. But sometimes after several hours of immersion we lift our heads and look around, suddenly struck by the quiet, the absence of others. In this situation, we are suffering from reading-induced loneliness. The solution is to read in the company of other people __(B) who__ are reading - whether in a public space such as a café or a library, or in your own home, with your reading friend or partner at the other end of the sofa. Next time you look up, you'll see someone else similarly __(C) immersing__, and you won't feel alone at all. Reading can be sociable. Consider joining a reading group __(D) in which__ everybody takes turns reading aloud from a novel. Reading a book collaboratively __(E) is__ a wonderful way to share an otherwise internal and solitary experience.

passageText: We all enjoy the pleasure of being left alone with a good book. But sometimes after several hours of immersion we lift our heads and look around, suddenly struck by the quiet, the absence of others. In this situation, we are suffering from reading-induced loneliness. The solution is to read in the company of other people who are reading - whether in a public space such as a café or a library, or in your own home, with your reading friend or partner at the other end of the sofa. Next time you look up, you'll see someone else similarly immersed, and you won't feel alone at all. Reading can be sociable. Consider joining a reading group in which everybody takes turns reading aloud from a novel. Reading a book collaboratively is a wonderful way to share an otherwise internal and solitary experience.

answerStage.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
answerStage.answerDesign: 정답 문장인 'The literary rendering of the original novel is as much an invention as the digital rendering of its fantastical creatures.'에서 주어의 핵심 명사는 동명사 단수 형태인 'rendering'입니다. 이를 원형 'is'에서 복수형 'are'로 변형하여 수일치 오류를 발생시킵니다. 수식어구 'of the original novel'의 명사 'novel' 역시 단수 명사이므로, 단순 근접 수일치 착각을 유도하는 것이 아니라, 문장 전체의 주어를 동명사구(The literary rendering ~)가 아닌 다른 복수 개념으로 잘못 파악하게 유도하는 고난도 구조입니다. 다른 방식으로 해석하더라도 주어 뒤의 동사는 절대 복수형 'are'를 취할 수 없으므로 명백한 비문입니다.

answer.surroundingText: The literary rendering of the original novel is as much an invention as the digital rendering of its fantastical creatures.

answerStage.explanation: 문장의 주어는 'The literary rendering of the original novel'로, 단수 명사인 'rendering'이 핵심 주어입니다. 따라서 동사는 복수형인 are가 아니라, 단수형 동사인 is가 와야 올바릅니다. 주어 뒤에 전치사구 수식어(of the original novel)가 붙어 주어와 동사의 거리가 멀어졌을 때 단수·복수의 수일치를 정확히 파악해야 하는 고난도 문제입니다.

markedExpressions.label: (C)

markedExpressions.label: (D)

markedExpressions.label: (E)

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 타동사 acknowledge의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끌며, 뒤에 완전한 절(technology can exist ~)이 이어지므로 접속사 'that'은 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 대명사 something useful을 뒤에서 후치 수식하는 과거분사이며, 수식을 받는 대상이 '정신에 의해 만들어지는' 수동 관계이므로 'produced'는 올바릅니다.

wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 문장의 주어 핵이 단수 명사인 rendering이므로, 수식어구(of the original novel)를 원천 차단하고 단수 동사인 'is'로 일치시킨 수일치는 정확합니다.

question.explanation: 이 문장은 조동사 can에 세 개의 동사원형 change, alter, 그리고 enable이 등위접속사 or를 통해 병렬 구조로 연결되어 있습니다. 따라서 세 번째 동사인 (B) enabling은 적절하지 않으며, 조동사 can의 지배를 받는 동사원형인 enable로 고쳐야 합니다. 문장 전체의 뼈대를 파악하여 조동사에 걸리는 병렬 요소들을 끝까지 추적해야 해결할 수 있는 수능형 고난도 문항입니다.
keyPoints: (B) 병렬 구조 — 조동사 can 뒤에 연결되는 복수의 동사원형 형태 일치 유도
(C) 분사의 태 능동 vs 수동 — 후치 수식을 받는 명사와의 수동 의미 관계 판정
(E) 주어-동사 수일치 — 주어의 핵심 명사 핵을 찾아 수식어에 현혹되지 않고 동사 수 일치
question.passageWithMarkers: We tend to think of technology as shiny tools and gadgets. Even if we acknowledge __(A) that__ technology can exist in disembodied form, such as software, we tend not to include in this category paintings, literature, music, dance, poetry, and the arts in general. But we should. If a thousand lines of letters in UNIX qualifies as a technology (the computer code for a web page), then a thousand lines of letters in English (Hamlet) must qualify as well. They both can change our behavior, alter the course of events, or __(B) enabling__ future inventions. A Shakespeare sonnet and a Schubert symphony, then, are in the same category as Google's search engine and the smartphone: They are something useful __(C) produced__ by a mind. We can't separate out the multiple overlapping technologies __(D) responsible__ for a Lord of the Rings movie. The literary rendering of the original novel __(E) is__ as much an invention as the digital rendering of its fantastical creatures. Both are useful works of the human imagination. Both influence audiences powerfully. Both are technological.

passageText: We tend to think of technology as shiny tools and gadgets. Even if we acknowledge that technology can exist in disembodied form, such as software, we tend not to include in this category paintings, literature, music, dance, poetry, and the arts in general. But we should. If a thousand lines of letters in UNIX qualifies as a technology (the computer code for a web page), then a thousand lines of letters in English (Hamlet) must qualify as well. They both can change our behavior, alter the course of events, or enable future inventions. A Shakespeare sonnet and a Schubert symphony, then, are in the same category as Google's search engine and the smartphone: They are something useful produced by a mind. We can't separate out the multiple overlapping technologies responsible for a Lord of the Rings movie. The literary rendering of the original novel is as much an invention as the digital rendering of its fantastical creatures. Both are useful works of the human imagination. Both influence audiences powerfully. Both are technological.

passageText: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information - a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.

answer.surroundingText: It doesn't take up any more time than it would when done with your phone pressed to your ear.

answerStage.explanation: when 뒤에 이어지는 분사구문에서 주절의 주어인 'it'(빨래를 하는 것, doing the laundry)과의 관계를 파악해야 합니다. 빨래를 하는 행동은 인간에 의해 '수행되는(done)' 수동의 대상이므로 과거분사 done이 오는 것이 알맞습니다. 능동의 형태를 나타내는 현재분사 doing을 쓰면 주어가 능동적으로 행동하는 의미가 되거나 목적어가 필요한데 뒤에 목적어가 없으므로 문법상 틀린 표현이 됩니다.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The fast pace of today's lifestyle has us piling one thing on top of another.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Give your whole focus to what you're doing at the moment no matter what it is.

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Listen to the sound of the water as it fills the washing machine and feel the clothes in your hand.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: It doesn't take up any more time than it would when done with your phone pressed to your ear.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The same applies to your work. Focus on one task at a time, and you'll accomplish each task better, and probably faster.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): has는 문장 전체의 주어인 'The fast pace of today's lifestyle'에 대응하는 본동사(정동사) 자리이며, 3인칭 단수 현재 시제에 맞게 올바르게 쓰였습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): what은 전치사 to의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끌며, 선행사가 없고 뒤에 이어지는 doing의 목적어가 비어 있는 불완전한 문장을 이끌고 있으므로 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): fills는 접속사 as가 이끄는 부사절 내에서 단수 대명사 주어인 it(the water)에 수일치하여 단수형 동사로 쓰인 정동사로 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): applies는 단수 명사 주어인 'The same'에 대응하며 일치하는 3인칭 단수형 동사로, '적용되다'라는 의미의 자동사로 알맞게 쓰였습니다.

question.explanation: when 뒤에 이어지는 분사구문에서 주절의 주어인 'it'(빨래를 하는 것, doing the laundry)과의 관계를 파악해야 합니다. 빨래를 하는 행동은 인간에 의해 '수행되는(done)' 수동의 대상이므로 과거분사 done이 오는 것이 알맞습니다. 능동의 형태를 나타내는 현재분사 doing을 쓰면 주어가 능동적으로 행동하는 의미가 되거나 목적어가 필요한데 뒤에 목적어가 없으므로 문법상 틀린 표현이 됩니다. 따라서 doing을 수동의 의미를 나타내는 과거분사 done으로 고쳐야 합니다.
keyPoints: (D) 분사구문의 능동 vs 수동 — 생략된 주어와의 의미 관계 및 목적어 유무로 판정
(A) 정동사 vs 준동사 — 주절을 완결할 정동사의 필요성 판단
(B) 관계대명사  what — 뒤에 불완전한 격의 절을 이끌며 선행사가 없을 때의 쓰임
question.passageWithMarkers: The fast pace of today's lifestyle __(A) has__ us piling one thing on top of another. But you should know that multitasking doesn't save any time. Very often, multitasking only slows you down, contrary to popular belief. Give your whole focus to __(B) what__ you're doing at the moment no matter what it is. While doing the laundry, just do the laundry: Listen to the sound of the water as it __(C) fills__ the washing machine and feel the clothes in your hand. It doesn't take up any more time than it would when __(D) doing__ with your phone pressed to your ear. The same __(E) applies__ to your work. Focus on one task at a time, and you'll accomplish each task better, and probably faster.

passageText: The fast pace of today's lifestyle has us piling one thing on top of another. But you should know that multitasking doesn't save any time. Very often, multitasking only slows you down, contrary to popular belief. Give your whole focus to what you're doing at the moment no matter what it is. While doing the laundry, just do the laundry: Listen to the sound of the water as it fills the washing machine and feel the clothes in your hand. It doesn't take up any more time than it would when done with your phone pressed to your ear. The same applies to your work. Focus on one task at a time, and you'll accomplish each task better, and probably faster.

answerStage.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
answerStage.answerDesign: 정답 문장 인용: 'The moment that occurs, the rest of the penguins watch with anticipation to see what happens next.'에서 원문 'occurs'를 'is occurred'로 변형하여 수동태 오류를 만듭니다. 'occur'는 자동사이므로 수동태로 쓰일 수 없으며 'is occurred'는 명백한 비문입니다. 'that'은 관계부사 대용 혹은 동격 접속사처럼 쓰여 'The moment (when/that) that occurs' 구조를 취하고 있으며, 여기서 'occurs'의 주어는 'that(그것, 즉 앞서 언급한 뛰어들기)'입니다. 다른 해석을 적용하더라도 자동사인 occur의 수동태는 절대 성립하지 않으므로 오답 논란이 없습니다.

answer.surroundingText: The moment that occurs, the rest of the penguins watch with anticipation to see what happens next.

answerStage.explanation: ‘The moment (that) ~’ 구문에서 ‘that’은 앞서 언급한 한 마리의 펭귄이 먼저 물속으로 뛰어드는 사건을 가리키는 대명사 주어입니다. 이 주어 뒤에서 술어 동사 역할을 하는 ‘occur’는 대표적인 자동사로, 목적어를 취하지 않기 때문에 수동태(be occurred)로 나타낼 수 없습니다. 따라서 능동태 형태인 단수 동사 ‘occurs’로 고쳐야 올바른 문장이 됩니다.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: There is a critical factor that determines whether your choice will influence that of others: the visible consequences of the choice.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: There is the leopard seal, for one, which likes to have penguins for a meal.

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: What is an Adélie to do? The penguins' solution is to play the waiting game.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The moment that occurs, the rest of the penguins watch with anticipation to see what happens next.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: One penguin's destiny alters the fate of all the others.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 앞에 나온 단수 명사인 your choice를 대신하여 지시하는 대명사로서 단수형인 that을 사용한 것은 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 선행사인 the leopard seal을 부연 설명하는 주격 관계대명사의 계속적 용법으로 쓰인 which는 어법상 맞습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 문장의 주어인 The penguins' solution에 호응하는 정동사(본동사) 자리로, 단수 수일치가 이루어진 현재형 동사 is의 사용은 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 주절의 동사구인 watch with anticipation 뒤에서 목적(~하기 위하여)을 타내는 부사적 용법의 to부정사구이므로 준동사 형태로 올바르게 쓰였습니다.

question.explanation: 주어와 동사의 수일치를 묻는 문항입니다. 해당 문장의 주어 핵은 3인칭 단수 명사인 'One penguin's destiny'이므로, 이에 대치되는 현재 시제의 술어 동사는 단수 동사 형태인 'alters'가 되어야 합니다. 복수형태인 'alter'는 주어의 수와 일치하지 않는 비문이므로, 'alters'로 고쳐야 올바릅니다.
keyPoints: (E) 주어와 동사의 수일치 — 3인칭 단수 주어 뒤에는 단수형 현재 동사 사용
(A) 대명사의 일치 — 앞의 명사가 단수(choice)이므로 지시대명사 that 선택
(B) 관계대명사의 계속적 용법 — 선행사를 선별하여 수식하는 주격 관계사 확인
question.passageWithMarkers: There is a critical factor __(A) that__ determines whether your choice will influence that of others: the visible consequences of the choice. Take the case of the Adélie penguins. They are often found strolling in large groups toward the edge of the water in search of food. Yet danger awaits in the icy-cold water. There is the leopard seal, for one, __(B) which__ likes to have penguins for a meal. What __(C) is__ an Adélie to do? The penguins' solution is to play the waiting game. They wait and wait and wait by the edge of the water until one of them gives up and jumps in. The moment that occurs, the rest of the penguins watch with anticipation __(D) to see__ what happens next. If the pioneer survives, everyone else will follow suit. If it perishes, they'll turn away. One penguin's destiny __(E) alter__ the fate of all the others. Their strategy, you could say, is "learn and live."

passageText: There is a critical factor that determines whether your choice will influence that of others: the visible consequences of the choice. Take the case of the Adélie penguins. They are often found strolling in large groups toward the edge of the water in search of food. Yet danger awaits in the icy-cold water. There is the leopard seal, for one, which likes to have penguins for a meal. What is an Adélie to do? The penguins' solution is to play the waiting game. They wait and wait and wait by the edge of the water until one of them gives up and jumps in. The moment that occurs, the rest of the penguins watch with anticipation to see what happens next. If the pioneer survives, everyone else will follow suit. If it perishes, they'll turn away. One penguin's destiny alters the fate of all the others. Their strategy, you could say, is "learn and live."

answerStage.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
answerStage.answerDesign: 정답 문장인 'We call people we haven't spoken to in ages, hoping that one small effort will erase the months and years of distance we've created.'에서 분사구문 이끄는 현재분사를 과거분사인 hoped로 변형합니다. 대상인 주어 'we'가 '바라는' 능동적 주체이므로 분사구문은 능동의 현재분사 형태인 'hoping'이 되어야 하며, 수동 의미의 'hoped'는 문맥상 비문입니다. 다른 해석(예: 동사의 과거형)으로 보더라도 뒤에 목적어 절(that one small effort...)이 바로 이어지며 문맥 내에서 전혀 성립하지 않으므로 명백한 오류입니다.

answer.surroundingText: We call people we haven't spoken to in ages, hoping that one small effort will erase the months and years of distance we've created.

answerStage.explanation: 문맥상 전화를 거는 행위자인 'we'가 '하나의 작은 노력이 우리가 만들어낸 몇 달과 몇 년의 거리감을 지워줄 것을 바라는' 능동적인 주체이므로 분사구문의 형태는 현재분사(hoping)가 되어야 어법상 적절합니다. 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거분사인 hoped는 뒤에 목적어절(that ~)을 가질 수 없으며 의미상으로도 부적절합니다.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: We call people we haven't spoken to in ages, hoping that one small effort will erase the months and years of distance we've created.

markedExpressions.label: (C)

markedExpressions.label: (D)

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 주격 관계대명사로서 선행사인 'the distance'를 수식하며, 뒤에 주어가 없는 불완전한 문장(has formed)이 이어지므로 어법상 올바른 쓰임입니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 문장의 주어인 'relationships'(관계)는 유지되는 대상이므로, 수동태 'aren't kept'로 표현하는 것이 자연스럽고 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 명사절(that절) 내의 주어인 'not too much time'이 단수 취급되므로, 단수 동사인 'goes'로 수일치시킨 것은 어법상 올바릅니다.

question.explanation: 주절의 주어 'We'가 전화를 거는 행위와 동시에 희망하는 능동적 주체이므로, 분사구문의 술어는 능동을 나타내는 현재분사여야 합니다. 또한 뒤에 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절 'that one small effort...'가 이어지고 있으므로 목적어를 취할 수 없는 과거분사는 들어갈 수 없습니다. 따라서 'hoped'를 'hoping'으로 고쳐야 어법상 올바른 문장이 됩니다.
keyPoints: (B) 분사구문의 능동 vs 수동 — 의미상 주어와의 능동 관계 및 뒤에 오는 목적어절 유무로 판정
(A) 관계대명사의 격과 역할 — 선행사 수식과 불완전한 절 구조 확인
(D) 주어-동사 수일치 — 셀 수 없는 명사 주어에 따른 단수동사 일치
question.passageWithMarkers: We tend to go long periods of time without reaching out to the people we know. Then, we suddenly take notice of the distance __(A) that__ has formed and we scramble to make repairs. We call people we haven't spoken to in ages, __(B) hoped__ that one small effort will erase the months and years of distance we've created. However, this rarely works: relationships __(C) aren't kept__ up with big one-time fixes. They're kept up with regular maintenance, like a car. In our relationships, we have to make sure that not too much time __(D) goes__ by between oil changes, so to speak. This isn't to say that you shouldn't bother calling someone just because it's been a while since you've spoken; just that it's more ideal not __(E) to let__ yourself fall out of touch in the first place. Consistency always brings better results.

passageText: We tend to go long periods of time without reaching out to the people we know. Then, we suddenly take notice of the distance that has formed and we scramble to make repairs. We call people we haven't spoken to in ages, hoping that one small effort will erase the months and years of distance we've created. However, this rarely works: relationships aren't kept up with big one-time fixes. They're kept up with regular maintenance, like a car. In our relationships, we have to make sure that not too much time goes by between oil changes, so to speak. This isn't to say that you shouldn't bother calling someone just because it's been a while since you've spoken; just that it's more ideal not to let yourself fall out of touch in the first place. Consistency always brings better results.

answerStage.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
answerStage.answerDesign: 정답 문장인 'What if the biggest thing keeping us from doing what matters is the false assumption that it has to take huge effort?'에서 주어인 the biggest thing을 수식하는 현재분사구 keeping us from doing what matters의 분사(keeping)를 정동사인 keeps로 왜곡합니다. 이 자리에서 keeps를 쓰면, 'What if the biggest thing keeps us...' 뒤에 본동사인 is가 존재하여 한 문장에 두 개의 정동사가 연결사 없이 충돌하는 비문이 됩니다. keeps 뒤에 접속사가 와서 구성을 바꾸지 않는 한, 문장의 구조적 뼈대를 관장하는 본동사 is 앞의 명사구를 수식하는 준동사(분사) 자리가 확보되어야 하므로 keeping이 문법적으로 유일하게 올바릅니다.

answer.surroundingText: What if the biggest thing keeping us from doing what matters is the false assumption that it has to take huge effort?

answerStage.explanation: 문장의 주어는 the biggest thing이며, 본동사는 뒤에 나오는 is입니다. 따라서 주어 명사를 수식하고 목적어와 전치사구를 취하는 수식어 자리에는 정동사가 아닌 준동사(현재분사)가 와야 합니다. 정동사 형태인 keeps를 쓰면 한 문장에 정동사가 두 개(keeps와 is) 존재하게 되어 비문이 되므로, 명사구 수식 역할을 담당하는 현재분사 keeping으로 고쳐야 어법상 올바릅니다.

passageText: You already have a business and you're about to launch your blog so that you can sell your product. Unfortunately, here is where a 'business mind' can be a bad thing. Most people believe that to have a successful business blog promoting a product, they have to stay strictly 'on the topic.' If all you're doing is shamelessly promoting your product, then who is going to want to read the latest thing you're writing about? passageText: Many people take the commonsense view that color is an objective property of things, or of the light that bounces off them. They say a tree's leaves are green because they reflect green light - a greenness that is just as real as the leaves. Others argue that color doesn't inhabit the physical world at all but exists only in the eye or mind of the viewer. They maintain that if a tree fell in a forest and no one was there to see it, its leaves would be colorless - and so would everything else. They say there is no such thing as color; there are only the people who see it. Both positions are, in a way, correct. Color is objective and subjective - "the place," as Paul Cézanne put it, "where our brain and the universe meet." Color is created when light from the world is registered by the eyes and interpreted by the brain.

passageText: Unfortunately, many people don't take personal responsibility for their own growth. Instead, they simply run the race laid out for them. They do well enough in school to keep advancing. Maybe they manage to get a good job at a well-run company. But so many think and act as if their learning journey ends with college. They have checked all the boxes in the life that was laid out for them and now lack a road map describing the right ways to move forward and continue to grow. In truth, that's when the journey really begins. When school is finished, your growth becomes voluntary. Like healthy eating habits or a regular exercise program, you need to commit to it and devote thought, time, and energy to it. Otherwise, it simply won't happen - and your life and career are likely to stop progressing as a result.

passageText: A lovely technique for helping children take the first steps towards creating their own, unique story, is to ask them to help you complete a story before you tell it. One story I have done this with frequently is a tale I call Benno and the Beasts. It is based on a story called St. Benno and the Frog, found in an old book by Helen Waddell. In the original, the saint meets a frog in a marsh and tells it to be quiet in case it disturbs his prayers. Later, he regrets this, in case God was enjoying listening to the sound of the frog. I invite children to think of different animals for the saint to meet and different places for him to meet them. I then tell them the story including their own ideas. It is a most effective way of involving children in the art of creating stories and they love hearing their ideas used.

passageText: The whole of human society operates on knowing the future weather. For example, farmers in India know when the monsoon rains will come next year and so they know when to plant the crops. passageText: Whether or not we can catch up on sleep - on the weekend, say - is a hotly debated topic among sleep researchers; the latest evidence suggests that while it isn't ideal, it might help. When Peter Liu, a UCLA sleep researcher, brought chronically sleep-restricted people into the lab for a weekend of sleep during which they slept about 10 hours per night, they showed improvements in the ability of insulin to process blood sugar. That suggests that catch-up sleep may undo some but not all of the damage that sleep deprivation causes, which is encouraging given how many adults don't get the hours they need each night. Still, Liu isn't ready to endorse the habit of sleeping less and making up for it later. "It's like telling people you only need to eat healthy during the weekends, but during the week you can eat whatever you like," he says.

markedExpressions.surroundingText: If someone asked you what you thought of a movie or your dinner, you might respond: "It was fine."

markedExpressions.label: (C)

wrongOptionExplanations.(B): asked의 직접목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끄는 의문대명사 'what'으로, 전치사 of의 목적어가 비어 있으므로 문법적으로 적절합니다.

question.explanation: 주절의 문장 골격을 완성할 정동사가 필요한 자리입니다. if-절 등의 종속절을 제외한 주절에서 문장의 서술어 역할을 하는 진짜 동사가 존재해야 합니다. 'Choosing'으로 쓰게 되면 문장에 정동사가 없는 비문법적 상태가 됩니다. 따라서 명령문의 형태가 되어야 하므로 준동사가 아닌 동사원형 'Choose'로 고쳐야 합니다.

passageText: A god called Moinee was defeated by a rival god called Dromerdeener in a terrible battle up in the stars. Moinee fell out of the stars down to Tasmania to die. question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.surroundingText: The point to remember is that sometimes in arguments the other person is trying to get you to be angry.

markedExpressions.label: (C)

markedExpressions.surroundingText: A remark may be made to cause your anger, but responding with a cool answer that focuses on the issue raised is likely to be most effective.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): the first things를 수식하는 과거분사구의 일부로, '잃게 되는 첫 번째 것들'이라는 수동의 의미관계를 나타내므로 과거분사 'lost'는 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 동사 try의 목적어로 쓰인 준동사구 내에서, 사역의 의미를 가지는 'get + 목적어 + to부정사' 구조를 이끌어 목적격보어 자리에 'to be'를 취하고 있으므로 'to get'은 어법상 올바른 쓰임입니다.

question.passageWithMarkers: We all know that tempers are one of the first things __(A) lost__ in many arguments. It's easy to say one should keep cool, but how do you do it? The point to remember is that sometimes in arguments the other person is trying __(B) to get__ you to be angry. They may be saying things that are intentionally __(C) designed__ to annoy you. They know that if they get you to lose your cool you'll say something that sounds foolish; you'll simply get angry and then it will be impossible for you to win the argument. So don't fall for it. passageText: We all know that tempers are one of the first things lost in many arguments. It's easy to say one should keep cool, but how do you do it? The point to remember is that sometimes in arguments the other person is trying to get you to be angry. They may be saying things that are intentionally designed to annoy you. They know that if they get you to lose your cool you'll say something that sounds foolish; you'll simply get angry and then it will be impossible for you to win the argument. So don't fall for it. A remark may be made to cause your anger, but responding with a cool answer that focuses on the issue raised is likely to be most effective. Indeed, any attentive listener will admire the fact that you didn't "rise to the bait."

passageText: We say to ourselves: “There is plenty of time. I’ll manage somehow or other when the time comes for action.” We are rather proud of our ability to meet emergencies. So we do not plan and take precautions to prevent emergencies from arising. It is too easy to drift through school and college, taking the traditional, conventional studies that others take, following the lines of least resistance, electing “snap courses,” and going with the crowd. It is too easy to take the attitude: “First I will get my education and develop myself, and then I will know better what I am fitted to do for a life work.” And so we drift, driven by the winds of circumstance, tossed about by the waves of tradition and custom. Eventually, most men find they must be satisfied with “any port in a storm.” Sailors who select a port because they are driven to it have scarcely one chance in a thousand of dropping anchor in the right one.
